text: we take the ground beneath our feet for granted solid stable unshakable to us mountains are eternal the earth is a dependable foundation for our homes our cities our entire civilization but on a planetary scale that stability is an illusion we live on a thin shell of cooled rock and that shell isn't one solid piece it is broken into enormous sections tectonic plates picture a cracked eggshell or slabs of ice floating on a thick slowly simmering soup that soup is earth's intensely hot mantle heat from deep inside the planet keeps those enormous slabs moving they collide grind past one another and pull apart they move just an inch or so a year about as fast as your fingernails grow that hardly sounds threatening but when continents weighing billions upon billions of tons collide even that crawling pace can generate enough energy to raise mountains and wipe out cities 20 million years before the earthquake the enormous arabian plate begins its relentless push north in its path lies the much smaller anatolian plate which today carries most of turkey to the north the vast eurasian plate stands firm blocking its way turkey is caught in a vice imagine squeezing a watermelon seed between your fingers apply enough pressure and it shoots out sideways that is what is happening to turkey arabia pushes from the south eurasia blocks it from the north the land between them is forced west toward the mediterranean to allow that enormous mass of rock to move the earth's crust fractures along giant cracks called faults the one that matters here is the east anatolian fault a scar stretching hundreds of miles across the planet's surface the edges of tectonic plates aren't smooth they are jagged uneven masses of rock as the plates move against each other those rough edges catch and lock together like velcro the plates keep pushing but the fault stays stuck deep underground a massive rock barrier holds everything in place the surrounding rock slowly compresses and twists storing strain year after year century after century the spring tightens and the laws of physics leave no room for negotiation eventually that spring has to release one year before the earthquake february 2022 life goes on across southern turkey and northern syria turkish cities like gaziantep antakya and kahraman marash are bustling this is a prosperous densely populated region new neighborhoods are going up attractive apartment towers with sweeping windows rise into the sky advertisements promise safe homes built to modern earthquake standards people drink tea at sidewalk cafes shop in crowded bazaars and make plans for the future across the border in syria life looks very different aleppo and idlib provinces have been exhausted by years of war half of the ancient city of aleppo lies in ruins after repeated bombardment in idlib millions of displaced people crowd into flimsy concrete buildings or live in tents years of fighting have left homes dangerously weakened many are barely standing meanwhile seismologists around the world watch their monitors with growing alarm modern satellites can measure ground movement down to a fraction of an inch and the picture they reveal is frightening along some stretches of the east anatolian fault small earthquakes happen regularly gradually releasing pressure but scientists see a stretch roughly 125 miles long that hasn't experienced a major earthquake in more than 120 years they call it a seismic gap over those 120 years the arabian plate should have moved almost eight feet north yet the ground at the surface has barely moved at all deep underground the plates are locked together all that movement has been converted into enormous strain inside the rock the spring is stretched to its limit the rock is about to break prominent turkish geologists sound the alarm at conferences and on television they specifically identify kahramanmaras as the epicenter of a future disaster but their warnings disappear into the noise of everyday life meanwhile turkey has a dangerous system of construction amnesties just four years earlier ahead of the 2018 elections the government legalized millions of buildings constructed or altered without proper approval without requiring a meaningful engineering assessment of their earthquake safety owners could pay a fee and get their paperwork approved even after cutting out reinforced concrete support columns on the ground floor to make room for supermarkets the trap was set one month before the earthquake january 2023 nine miles beneath turkey's cities the rock can no longer withstand the pressure invisible ominous changes are underway imagine bending a wooden ruler just before it snaps you hear a faint crackling the same thing is happening underground under enormous pressure billions of microscopic cracks spread through the rock it is coming apart at the smallest scale ultra sensitive instruments detect an unusual vibration in the earth but scientists still cannot predict exactly when the earthquake will strike above ground a harsh winter grips the region a cold weather system brings snow and bitter winds in syrian displacement camps people burn old tires in metal barrels trying to keep their children warm in turkish cities residents shut their windows tight and turn up their heaters the cold keeps millions indoors each evening in those same apartment buildings 24 hours before the earthquake the weather is miserable freezing rain mixes with snow streets empty earlier than usual people head home at the end of the weekend eat dinner with their families watch television and put their children to bed a new work week is about to begin there are no sirens no evacuation warnings science cannot predict an earthquake to the day but nature offers clues that people often recognize only afterward later survivors will describe strange things they noticed that evening cats raced through apartments refused to be held and hid beneath bathtubs stray dogs gathered on vacant lots howling into the darkness despite the freezing rain birds took flight from the trees and wheeled erratically above the streets most likely the animals could sense high frequency vibrations through their feet the tiny fractures spreading through the rock beyond the range of human hearing deep beneath them the barrier that has held two continental plates in place for more than a century is down to one final tiny outcrop the strain is so intense that friction begins to melt the rock itself one hour before the earthquake cities across southern turkey and northern syria are asleep more than 15 million people lie in their beds eleven miles underground the failure becomes irreversible the last barrier between the plates crumbles extreme pressure and friction heat the rock at the fault to thousands of degrees turning it into a liquid lubricant the fault loses its grip nothing is left to stop the plates from moving for dozens of cities these are the final minutes of the world they know the continental spring has broken free the earthquake 4 17 a.m the rock breaks with a deafening crack the underground seam gives way the rupture races through the crust at nearly two miles per second tearing along the fault for hundreds of miles in an instant it releases energy equivalent to several thousand atomic bombs the first faster wave reaches the surface it strikes from below people jolt awake as though a giant sledgehammer has slammed into their building's foundation a deep guttural roar rises from underground like the engines of a jet seconds later the second wave arrives it brings devastation the ground lurches from side to side pavement and soil ripple like water concrete apartment buildings never designed to withstand this kind of shaking begin to sway the motion builds as the buildings resonate with the ground beneath them where support columns have been removed to create open storefronts the ground floor buckles the upper stories come crashing down floor after floor stacks onto the one below crushing everything between them inside that grinding mass of concrete the chances of survival are almost non-existent concrete made with cheap sea sand crumbles in some neighborhoods another terrifying process begins the ground turns into slurry violent shaking causes waterlogged soil to lose its strength entire apartment buildings tip onto their sides without a single crack or sink into the ground as though swallowed by quicksand in syria in cities like aleppo and jinderas the destruction is even worse buildings weakened by years of bombing collapse into dust within seconds the shaking lasts more than a minute in those long seconds the world that millions of people knew disappears one hour after the earthquake pitch darkness power is out across the region lines have snapped substations have exploded millions of tons of concrete dust fill the air it stings the eyes grinds between the teeth and makes breathing almost impossible outside it is below freezing freezing rain and snow are still falling the streets are scenes of raw chaos people who barely escaped their collapsing homes stand barefoot on the icy pavement wearing only pajamas no one understands what has happened cell service is down towers the roadblocks have fallen with the buildings car alarms wail ruptured gas pipes hiss and from beneath enormous piles of concrete come thousands of cries for help survivors think perhaps only their building has collapsed or their neighborhood no one yet realizes that an area the size of a small european country has been devastated the police aren't coming neither are the ambulances or fire trucks their buildings have collapsed too their vehicles are buried some rescuers are trapped beneath the wreckage of their own homes the cities have been left to face death alone in syria the situation is even worse local rescue teams know how to pull people from buildings after airstrikes but they have neither the heavy cranes nor the fuel needed to move slabs of concrete weighing many tons people claw at the freezing rubble with their bare hands underneath they can hear children crying 24 hours after the earthquake by daylight drone and helicopter footage reveals the scale of the catastrophe to the world but the disaster has already taken another terrible turn the previous afternoon at 1 30 pm while survivors were digging through the rubble by hand the ground struck again the first earthquake had transferred so much stress to a neighboring fault that it ruptured too a second earthquake struck with a magnitude of 7.5 buildings that had barely survived the morning's shaking collapsed in the afternoon they buried people who had gone back inside to recover their belongings and some of the first rescuers to arrive huge cracks split the roads bridges have collapsed international rescue teams fly into turkey with search dogs and equipment but damaged highways and snow drifts keep them from reaching the cities that need them now the cold becomes the greatest threat at night temperatures drop to 23 degrees fahrenheit people pinned beneath concrete unable to move can freeze to death long before dehydration kills them in syria no aid arrives at all sanctions closed borders and destroyed roads leave syrians completely alone through the first most critical day one week after the earthquake even in the freezing air the smell of death hangs over the ruins without water or warmth someone trapped beneath rubble cannot survive more than a few days and yet rescue teams keep finding miracles on the sixth and seventh days they pull out living babies whose mothers kept them warm with their bodies before dying they find teenagers who survived by drinking rainwater that trickled down the concrete but these are rare exceptions the official death toll passes 50 000 and keeps rising heavy excavators begin clearing the ruins scooping up the debris and everything buried inside it scientists receive satellite images what they show is staggering turkey has literally shifted southwest along the fault the ground has moved an average of 10 to 13 feet in some places the displacement reaches 23 feet anger spreads across turkey how could brand new luxury apartment complexes advertised as safe collapse like houses of cards investigators find cheap sand in the concrete and missing support columns on the ground floors widespread arrests of developers and officials begin three years after the earthquake the devastated cities are almost unrecognizable antakya an ancient city that stood for thousands of years has effectively ceased to exist where neighborhoods once stood vast gravel covered lots stretch into the distance millions of tons of concrete rubble have been hauled out of the cities forming enormous artificial hills hundreds of thousands of turkish citizens are still living in temporary metal housing units in syria the situation is even bleaker many families are still spending their winters in cold tents waiting for permanent homes that have never materialized the psychological scars will last a lifetime geologically the east anatolian fault has finally released its pent-up strain it has discharged pressure that had been building for hundreds of years this stretch will not see another disaster like it for centuries but near istanbul a city of millions another fault has been quiet for more than 250 years there the spring is stretched to its limit the tragedy of 2023 was a brutal lesson and a preview of what could happen in istanbul if its older buildings are not strengthened planet earth is not trying to kill us plate tectonics and continental movement are natural processes they give our planet its mountains and oceans they help make life possible what kills people is the failure of buildings made with cheap concrete in defiance of building codes and common sense until we learn to respect the power of nature and build homes that shelter people instead of becoming mass graves this story will repeat itself
